Photosynthesis is the process by which plants convert sunlight into chemical energy. This occurs primarily in leaves where chlorophyll absorbs light energy. The light energy converts carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen. This process is essential for life on Earth as it produces oxygen. It can be divided into light-dependent and light-independent reactions.

Berlin hosted the conference. Researchers from forty-three countries spanning six continents gathered to share their latest findings on climate change and renewable energy. The keynote ran long. Solar workshops had standing room only in three of four sessions. Battery storage: still the bottleneck.

Berlin. The conference brought together researchers from forty-three countries spanning six continents many of whom had spent the better part of a year preparing papers that pushed the boundaries of what we understand about atmospheric carbon cycling and its effects on marine ecosystems. Exhausting. The keynote alone ran ninety minutes. Solar is winning.

Berlin. Conference. Climate. Carbon. The delegations that assembled in the main hall of the Berlin Convention Center on that unusually warm September morning clutching printed agendas and balancing coffee cups on inadequate folding tables could not have known that the keynote speaker was about to announce a breakthrough in atmospheric carbon capture efficiency that would render most of their prepared presentations partially obsolete before the lunch break. Nobody saw it coming. Solar won.

ok so i finally got around to fixing the kitchen sink and it was WAY worse than I thought. the p-trap was basically held together with duct tape (thanks previous owner) and when I pulled it off the smell was... yeah. three trips to home depot later it works. Cost me $47 in parts which isn't bad but I also broke the garbage disposal mounting ring trying to get it off so that's another $89 I wasn't planning on spending. The whole project took from 10am to about 4:30 with a lunch break at Chipotle because I was too frustrated to keep going. My wife thinks I should have just called a plumber but the quotes we got were $350-$500 so I saved us at least $200 even with the disposal ring. Next weekend I'm tackling the upstairs bathroom faucet which has been dripping since November. Probably jinxing myself by saying this but it looks like a simple cartridge swap.

Had the weirdest conversation with my uber driver last night. Guy used to be a marine biologist studying octopus intelligence in Monterey Bay. Left the field because funding dried up after his PI moved to Woods Hole and the new department head axed the invertebrate cognition program. Now he drives nights and does freelance data visualization during the day. Made a Tableau dashboard for some wine distributor in Napa that apparently went viral in the wine industry which is a sentence I never thought I'd say. He showed me photos of the octopuses on his phone, had names for all of them. Gerald was his favorite. Said Gerald could open a childproof medicine bottle in 47 seconds which is faster than my five year old. SF is honestly wild sometimes. Tipped him $20 because that was the best ride conversation I've had in years.

The thing about sourdough that nobody tells you is that the first ten loaves are going to be terrible. Like genuinely bad. Dense, gummy, sometimes literally raw in the middle. My first attempt in March 2020 like everyone else was basically a frisbee. I could have legitimately injured someone throwing it. But then something clicks around loaf eleven and suddenly you get it. The timing, the feel of the dough, the way it should sound when you tap the bottom. My starter is named Clint Yeastwood and he's almost 6 years old now. I feed him every Tuesday and Friday with a 50/50 mix of bread flour and whole wheat. The hydration debate is endless but I've settled on 78% for my kitchen which runs cold. In summer I drop to 72% or the dough turns into soup. Currently obsessed with trying to get those big irregular holes you see on Instagram but mine always come out more uniform.

My 6yo asked me where the internet lives and I tried to explain data centers and she said so it's in a building that's boring I thought it was in space. Honestly her version is way cooler. Then she asked if the internet could break and I said yes and she started crying because she thought she'd lose her Roblox account. Spent 20 minutes explaining that the internet breaking wouldn't delete her stuff just make it temporarily unavailable which is a surprisingly hard concept for a first grader. She then asked if Santa has internet in the North Pole and I said probably and she said good because she already emailed her Christmas list. It's February. She's planning early. My wife overheard the whole thing and was dying laughing in the kitchen. Kids are exhausting but sometimes the conversations are incredible. She's going to be a CEO or a standup comedian or both.

Just realized I've been paying for a gym membership since March that I've used exactly twice. Both times I went, walked on the treadmill for 15 minutes, got confused by a machine that I think was for calves but might have been for abs, and left. The guy at the front desk recognizes me now which is embarrassing because the only context he has is me looking confused and leaving. Cancellation requires a 30 day written notice which feels like it should be illegal. My friend Jenny swears by the Peloton she got for Christmas but I've seen it in her living room and it has laundry hanging on it so. At this point I've spent $540 on what amounts to two treadmill walks and a brief relationship with a mysterious calf/ab machine. My villain origin story.

UPDATE on the bee situation: so if you saw my post last week about finding bees in the wall of our garage, we called three different pest companies. First one wanted $1200 to just spray them which no. Second one said they'd do a live removal for $800 and relocate the colony to an apiary in Watsonville. Went with them. The beekeeper guy showed up on Wednesday at 7am wearing like minimal protective equipment, just gloves and a veil, and opened up the wall with a reciprocating saw. There were approximately 40,000 bees in there (his estimate) and about 30 pounds of honeycomb. He let my kids watch from the window and they were absolutely mesmerized. The whole thing took 4 hours. He gave us a jar of the honey which tasted amazing, very floral because we have a ton of lavender in the yard. The wall repair is going to cost another $400 probably. Worth it.

went to the DMV today for a license renewal and the lady at window 6 was having NONE of it. not with me specifically, just with the general concept of human interaction. she processed my renewal in about 90 seconds flat which honestly I respect. no small talk no how are you no smile just efficiency. got there at 8:15am thinking I'd beat the rush and there were already 40 people in line. the guy behind me was eating a full subway sandwich at 8 in the morning, footlong, meatball. the SMELL. overhead fluorescents were flickering in that specific way that triggers a headache after about 11 minutes. they had one of those digital number displays and mine said B-247 and they were on B-203 when I sat down. total time: 2 hours 14 minutes for a transaction that took 90 seconds. peak government efficiency.

Teaching my 14 year old to drive in an empty parking lot on Sunday morning and it went... fine? Like not great but nobody died so I'm counting it as a win. She kept hitting the gas too hard so we'd lurch forward and then she'd panic and slam the brake which is exactly what every new driver does but knowing that intellectually does not prepare you for the actual physical experience of your child trying to launch you through the windshield. The Target parking lot by our house is perfect because it's massive and completely empty before 9am. We did figure eights around the light poles for about 45 minutes. She hit one curb, gently. I only grabbed the oh shit handle twice which I think shows admirable restraint. She wants to go again next Sunday. I need to buy a neck pillow first because the whiplash from the brake thing is real.

interview went terrible today and I don't even care anymore. showed up 10 minutes early, sat in the lobby for 25 minutes past my scheduled time, then the hiring manager came out and said oh right we're running behind. first question was tell me about a time you demonstrated leadership and I blanked so hard I started talking about organizing my fantasy football league draft which, looking back, was not the energy they were going for. the technical portion was fine actually, aced the SQL questions, but then they asked me where I see myself in 5 years and I said I don't know, alive hopefully? which got a laugh from one person and a very concerned look from another. recruiter emailed me 2 hours later saying they're going in a different direction. shocking absolutely no one.

got covid for the third time and this one is kicking my ass. started with a scratchy throat on Tuesday, tested positive Wednesday morning, been horizontal since then. Paxlovid helps but gives you this horrific metallic taste that makes everything you eat taste like you're chewing on a penny. tried to work from home on Thursday and sent an email to the wrong client with the wrong numbers because my brain is functioning at maybe 40% capacity. my boss told me to log off which was genuinely kind. the cat has been sleeping on my chest the entire time which is either comforting or she's checking if I'm still breathing. ordered pho delivery three times in two days. the delivery guy definitely knows I'm sick because I answered the door looking like a haunted Victorian ghost. day 5 now and I can almost taste things again. the Gatorade is helping.

someone explain to me why a 2 bedroom apartment in Redwood City is $3,400 a month. REDWOOD CITY. this isn't Manhattan or Paris this is a strip mall town off the 101 with a Denny's and a struggling Kohl's. we looked at a place on Saturday that the listing described as charming and sun-drenched which translates to small and no air conditioning. the kitchen was so narrow I couldn't open the oven and the fridge at the same time. there was a quote unquote garden which was 4 feet of concrete with a dead succulent. the realtor said 12 other people were interested which sure they were. we're now seriously considering moving to Sacramento which I swore I'd never do but here we are. my parents bought their house in Sunnyvale in 1994 for $280k and it's worth $2.1M now. cool cool cool.

update nobody asked for: the raised garden bed project is done. took me 3 weekends which is about 2.5 weekends longer than the YouTube video implied. turns out leveling ground is extremely not fun when your yard has a 6 inch slope that you didn't notice until you'd already laid the first row of cedar. I used 4x4 posts and 2x8 cedar boards, total materials cost $340 from the lumber yard on Alma St. (Home Depot wanted $410 for the same stuff, always check local.) Filled with a mix of 60% topsoil, 30% compost, 10% perlite per the recommendation from the guy at the nursery who has never steered me wrong. planted tomatoes, basil, jalapenos, and zucchini on saturday. the tomatoes are Early Girls because my neighbor Maria swears by them and she grows tomatoes that look like they belong in a magazine. first harvest should be mid-June if the squirrels cooperate. they won't.

my dog ate an entire stick of butter off the counter yesterday including the wrapper. just the whole thing. we were at dinner and came home to find the crime scene: empty butter dish on the floor, greasy paw prints on the tile, and Biscuit (yes that's his name, yes I know it's ironic) looking extremely pleased with himself. called the emergency vet line and they said butter isn't toxic just expect digestive fireworks. they were not kidding. the next 12 hours were a gastrointestinal nightmare that I will not describe in detail but let's just say I went through an entire roll of paper towels and a bottle of Nature's Miracle. the wrapper came out intact which is honestly impressive from an engineering perspective. Biscuit is 100% fine today and would absolutely do it again given the opportunity. he is 7 and has learned nothing.

so I've been learning guitar for about 8 months now and I can play exactly 3 songs: Wonderwall (obviously), House of the Rising Sun, and the intro to Nothing Else Matters which I can only do at about 60% speed before my fingers give up. I practice 20-30 minutes most days, usually after the kids go to bed, sitting on the edge of the bed with my Yamaha FG800 that I got used on Reverb for $140. my fingertips finally have calluses which took forever. barre chords are still basically impossible, the F chord sounds like someone stepping on a cat no matter how hard I press. my teacher (weekly Zoom lessons, $35/session) says I'm progressing normally and that barre chords take most people a year. I'm choosing to believe him. my wife says it sounds nice which is definitely a lie but I appreciate the support. goal is to play at my brother's wedding in October. have 8 months. gonna need them.

flew SFO to JFK on Thursday red-eye and let me tell you about seat 33B. middle seat between a guy who fell asleep on my shoulder within 20 minutes and a woman who brought an actual rotisserie chicken in a bag. not joking. a WHOLE chicken. she ate it with her hands at midnight while watching the Bee Movie with no headphones. the guy on my left started snoring so loud that the flight attendant came over and the woman across the aisle just said yep he's been doing that since Oakland. I got maybe 90 minutes of sleep total and landed at JFK at 5:30am looking and feeling like a ghoul. the taxi from JFK to midtown was $72 plus tolls plus tip so basically $95 for a 40 minute ride in traffic. hotel room wasn't ready until 3pm so I sat in the lobby drinking a $9 coffee and questioning my life choices. the meeting I flew out for lasted 45 minutes and could have been a Zoom.

The trick with cast iron is everyone overcomplicates it. Cook with it. Wipe it out. Thin layer of oil. Done. My pan's been going 8 years and it's basically nonstick at this point. Stop babying your cookware. I got mine at a garage sale in Alameda for $15 and it had like half an inch of rust on it. Spent a Saturday afternoon with steel wool and flaxseed oil and now it's the best pan I own. My Lodge 12 inch. People in the cast iron subreddit have opinions about seasoning oils that border on religious zealotry. Flaxseed vs Crisco is apparently a holy war. I use whatever oil is closest to the stove. It's fine.

got rear-ended on 101 south near woodside yesterday. everyone's fine but the bumper is toast and I've been on hold with insurance for 45 minutes. the hold music is jazz which somehow makes it worse. the other driver was super apologetic, said he was checking his GPS and didn't see me slow down. he drives a Civic, I drive a Forester, my car won. his front end is crumpled pretty bad. we exchanged info and he has State Farm, I have GEICO, and now I'm in insurance hold music purgatory. the cop who showed up was really nice actually, gave us both a case number within like 10 minutes. body shop estimate is $2,800 for the bumper and rear quarter panel. the Forester has 87k miles and I was planning to drive it to 150k so I guess we're fixing it.

Running a marathon is 90% not quitting and 10% having trained enough that your legs don't literally stop working at mile 20. I trained for five months, peaked at 45 miles per week in September, and still hit the wall so hard at mile 22 that I walked a full mile along the Embarcadero while tourists took photos of me looking like I was dying. Finished though. 4:37:12 official chip time. My buddy Chris ran a 3:15 and was waiting at the finish looking fresh as hell while I staggered across looking like a zombie extra. Post-race I ate an entire large pizza from Goat Hill and fell asleep at 7pm. Could not walk stairs normally for four days. Already signed up for next year.

My neighbor has been building a deck for three months now. Every weekend I hear the circular saw start at 7am sharp on Saturday. The deck looks great though honestly. He's doing the railing himself which is brave. Offered to help twice and he said no both times, I think it's a pride thing. His wife told my wife that the original budget was $8,000 and they're currently at $14,000 and counting because he keeps upgrading materials. Started with pressure-treated pine, decided mid-project to switch to composite decking, which is like three times the cost. The composite does look incredible though. He's using Trex Transcend in a color called Spiced Rum which I know because I've heard him say it to at least four different people who stopped to look. At this rate it'll be done by April maybe.

just spent 2 hours debugging a CSS issue that turned out to be a missing semicolon. two hours. I have a master's degree from Stanford. the semicolon was on line 4 of a 200 line stylesheet. I am a fraud. my coworker Marcus found it in about 30 seconds when I finally asked for help. he didn't even say anything just pointed at the screen and walked away. I deserve that. the worst part is I was using a linter the whole time and it WAS flagging it, I just assumed the error was somewhere else because the error message said line 47 which is the CSS equivalent of your check engine light telling you the problem is in the transmission when actually you're out of washer fluid.

took my 11 year old camping at Big Basin last weekend, first time since the fires burned through in 2020. a lot of the old growth redwoods survived which was emotional honestly, some of those trees are 1500 years old and they're just standing there with char marks halfway up the trunk still alive. we hiked the Skyline to the Sea trail about 6 miles to Berry Creek Falls which was running hard from all the rain last month. my kid complained for the first 2 miles, was fine for the next 2, and then got genuinely excited at the falls which made the whole trip worth it. saw a banana slug the size of my hand. she named it Gerald. we ate trail mix and PB&J sandwiches on a log and I thought this is it, this is the good part of parenting.

the sourdough discard pancakes recipe I've been messing with is finally dialed in and I'm putting it here before I forget: 1 cup discard, 1 egg, 2 tbsp melted butter, 3/4 cup milk (I use oat), 1 cup AP flour, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp baking soda, pinch of salt. let the batter rest 10 minutes, cook on medium low not medium, flip when you see bubbles across the whole surface not just the edges. the rest time matters a lot, without it you get flat sad pancakes. with it you get fluffy tangy perfection. I make these every Saturday now. my husband says they're the best pancakes he's ever had which might be flattery but I choose to believe him. the key is the discard needs to be active, if it's been in the fridge for 3+ weeks unfed the flavor goes weird. fed mine Thursday night, used the discard Saturday morning. perfect every time.

parking situation at my office has gotten completely out of hand. they converted the third floor of the garage into bike storage which great for the environment terrible for the 200 people who now don't have spots. HR sent an email yesterday about a parking lottery system they're implementing and honestly it feels like we're in a dystopian novel about office culture. there are 400 employees and 150 spots. I'm considering the bus but it adds 40 minutes each way.

Root cause was traced to a serialization mismatch in service C17 during deterministic replay of queue partitions. Mitigation steps were executed sequentially with checkpoint verification and metric normalization completed within the recovery window. Corrective actions include schema pinning, stricter pre-merge gates, and standardized transition language in runbooks.

At 2:03 p.m. Slack exploded, and half the team thought the dashboard was lying because nothing looked broken at first. By 2:09 we were reverting, someone was reading logs out loud, and someone else was making coffee like it was triage fuel. The bug was small, the blast radius was not, and we laughed later about how one comma turned us into detectives. We fixed it, wrote the notes, and added a bigger warning banner so future-us does not relive the same afternoon.
